Helium with a new and empty profile using `--user-data-dir` command line argument and it could not be reproduced there ### Description When Minimal URL is enabled, the Always show full URLs option should not prevent the address bar from showing only the hostname when unfocused. ### Crash ID _No response_ ### How to Reproduce? 1. On a fresh profile with Helium defaut settings, open this website: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page 2. If it is still focused, unfocus the URL bar by clicking anywhere in the page. 3. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page is displayed in the URL bar. 4. Now go to helium://settings/ 5. Enable this option: Minimal URL in the address bar 6. Switch back to the Wikipedia tab; now en.wikipedia.org is shown. 7. If you focus the URL bar by clicking in it, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page is displayed. 8. Now right click the URL bar and enable the Always show full URLs option; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page is displayed in the URL bar. 9. Unfocus the URL bar by clicking somewhere else: The full URL (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page) is still shown. ### Actual behavior When both "Minimal URL in the address bar" and "Always show full URLs" are enabled, the full URL is still shown when the address bar is unfocused, even though Minimal URL is enabled. ### Expected behavior The "Minimal URL in the address bar" option should still show only the minimal URL when the address bar is unfocused, while "Always show full URLs" should only affect the address bar when it is focused. ### Additional context _No Open Helium 0.16.2.1 2. Go to https://id.focusritegroup.com/ 3. On the Sign in page, enter any email (e.g. abc@gmail.com) 4. Click Continue 5. Tab becomes unresponsive and shows Error code: RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE ### Actual behavior The tab dies immediately after Continue. I get Chromium's "Aw, Snap" page. The link is broken even when trying to refresh or open in a new tab "Something went wrong while displaying this webpage." Error code: RESULT_CODE_KILLED_BAD_MESSAGE Chrome and Firefox work on the same flow.. ### Expected behavior Continue should go to the email passcode form, same as Chrome and Firefox. ### Additional context I looked at this in DevTools. Continue isn't failing the request. POST /a//login/api/v2/identifier returns 200 and the session cookie is there. After that, mfa-passcode.block-*.js loads and calls navigator.credentials.get({ otp: { transport: ["sms"] } }) because OTPCredential is on window. Helium already turns kWebOTP off in disable-non-standard-auth-features.patch (3e0448a6, from #2352). That looks like it only kills the service. The JS API is still there, the page calls it, and the tab dies. Launching with --disable-blink-features=WebOTP makes Continue work and I get the email passcode form. I don't think this is uBlock, third-party cookies, or Helium Noise. My guess is OTPCredential should just not exist when WebOTP is disabled. 0.16.2.1 **Helium Framework:** 152.0.7977.64 (`refs/branch-heads/7977@{#1891}`, cl `506c834ecceaa943c5f41e6cfe7f68acb5c45346`) **macOS:** 27.0 (Darwin 27.0.0), Apple Silicon **Channel:** stable, no flags (`--flag-switches-begin --flag-switches-end`) ## Symptom On certain authentication pages the window appears for a fraction of a second and then closes on its own. Nothing is shown, no error page. Seen on two unrelated sites: - `https://goguvenliodeme.bkm.com.tr/troy/approve` — a Turkish BKM/Troy 3-D Secure card-authentication page, reached as the 3DS step of a real card payment - `https://auth.agah.com` — an unrelated brokerage login page The same 3DS page works normally in Chrome. It is **intermittent** — on a later attempt the BKM payment completed successfully in Helium. Impact: this keeps recurring on login and payment-authentication pages, which are exactly the flows I cannot retry casually, so I end up having to switch to another browser mid-payment. ## This is not a crash I want to be explicit, because the artifacts below look like crash dumps and are not: - I watched the browser process across a reproduction of the failure. PID `63585` stayed alive the whole time (`ELAPSED 10:20`), and no new dump was written. The app is not being killed and no tab shows a sad-tab page. - There is no matching report in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/`. ## What is odd Helium's browser process writes a Crashpad minidump with exception code `0x43507378` → `'CPsx'`, Crashpad's simulated-exception marker (i.e. `DumpWithoutCrashing`, a caught bad state rather than a fatal fault). Four such dumps exist, and **all four are at the identical offset in the framework**, on both sites: | Dump | Time | Page in dump | `ptype` | Exception | Module + offset | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `2e5f6e51-…` | 2026-08-30 11:59 | `auth.agah.com` | browser | `'CPsx'` | `Helium Framework +0xb9c5150` | | `9c913ac1-…` | 2026-08-30 12:00 | `auth.agah.com` | browser | `'CPsx'` | `Helium Framework +0xb9c5150` | | `dbde0d9c-…` | 2026-08-31 17:02 | `goguvenliodeme.bkm.com.tr/troy/approve` | browser | `'CPsx'` | `Helium Framework +0xb9c5150` | | `8648f651-…` | 2026-08-31 17:04 | `goguvenliodeme.bkm.com.tr/troy/approve` | browser | `'CPsx'` | `Helium Framework +0xb9c5150` | Module bases differ across the dumps (ASLR), so the constant `+0xb9c5150` is a single code location, not an address coincidence. You should be able to symbolize that offset directly against the 152.0.7977.64 build. Two unrelated sites, the same user-visible failure, the same single offset, in the browser process. ## Caveats, stated honestly - The correlation is not perfect: during one reproduction of the failure, **no** dump was written at all. So the dump and the window-closing may be two symptoms of one cause rather than cause and effect. - The dumps are non-fatal — one browser process wrote a dump on Aug 30 and kept running for another 29 hours before writing the next one. - One older dump (2026-08-26, `6b809ef5-…`) is a genuine `EXC_BREAKPOINT` at a different offset (`+0x2742eb8`). issue in Chrome and it could not be reproduced there - [ ] I have tried reproducing this issue in ungoogled-chromium and it could not be reproduced there - [ ] I have tried reproducing this issue in Helium with a new and empty profile using `--user-data-dir` command line argument and it could not be reproduced there ### Description `chrome.enterprise.reportingPrivate.getContextInfo()` invokes its callback with `undefined` and no `runtime.lastError`, so Google's Endpoint Verification extension fails every sync and the device is never reported to Google Workspace. ### How to Reproduce? 1. Sign in to Helium with a Google Workspace account that has Endpoint Verification enabled. 2. Install the Endpoint Verification extension (`callobklhcbilhphinckomhgkigmfocg`) from the Chrome Web Store. 3. Open the extension popup and let it sync (or wait for the `SYNC_ALARM`). 4. Open the extension log (popup > "Show log", or the service worker console) and set the log level to DEBUG. 5. Every sync attempt ends with a `SEVERE` entry. ### Actual behavior Every sync fails with a `TypeError`: ``` [SyncService] [INFO] Syncing ... [SyncService] [SEVERE] Failed to Sync . Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'realtimeUrlCheckMode') [SyncService] [INFO] Finished sync (4). [UIModel] [DEBUG] Sync finished with error TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'realtimeUrlCheckMode'). [AlarmTimeoutManager] [INFO] Scheduling next sync in 9 minutes. [SyncService] [WARNING] Sync ended up with an error. One or more errors occurred. ``` This repeats every 9 to 11 minutes forever. The device is never registered, so any resource behind context-aware access stays blocked. The extension code that throws (`background_service_worker.js`, v1.140.0, deminified names kept as shipped): ```js // wrapper around the API getContextInfo() { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { chrome.enterprise.reportingPrivate.getContextInfo(d => { const e = chrome.runtime.lastError; e ? reject(new X(1, im, e.message || "Call to c.e.rP.getContextInfo failed.")) : resolve(d); }); }); } // consumer let b; try { b = yield a.Tm.get(); // resolves with undefined here } catch (e) { return uv.warn(`Error getting Browser Info. ${e.message}`), {}; } switch (b.realtimeUrlCheckMode) { /* TypeError: b is undefined */ } ``` The extension already handles a rejected call (it logs `Error getting Browser Info` and continues with `{}`). It does not handle a call that *succeeds* with no value, so the only way to reach this `TypeError` is a callback invoked with `undefined` while `chrome.runtime.lastError` is unset. ### Expected behavior `getContextInfo()` either resolves with a `ContextInfo` object (with `realtimeUrlCheckMode` set to `disabled`, since Safe Browsing is not built in) or fails with `chrome.runtime.lastError` set, so callers can fall back. Endpoint Verification syncs successfully and the device is reported to Google Workspace. ### Additional context Full OS version: macOS 26.6.1 (arm64). Likely related to `safe_browsing_mode=0` in `flags.gn` and the Safe Browsing build fixes. `patches/ungoogled-chromium/fix-building-without-safebrowsing.patch` touches exactly this API: ``` --- a/chrome/browser/extensions/api/enterprise_reporting_private/enterprise_reporting_private_api.cc +++ b/chrome/browser/extensions/api/enterprise_reporting_private/enterprise_reporting_private_api.cc @@ -267,16 +267,8 @@ api::enterprise_reporting_private::Conte signals.chrome_remote_desktop_app_blocked; info.os_firewall = ToInfoSettingValue(signals.os_firewall); info.system_dns_servers = std::move(signals.system_dns_servers); - switch (signals.realtime_url_check_mode) { - case enterprise_connectors::REAL_TIME_CHECK_DISABLED: info.realtime_url_check_mode = extensions::api:: enterprise_reporting_private::RealtimeUrlCheckMode::kDisabled; - break; ... ``` That hunk still assigns `realtime_url_check_mode`, so the field itself should be present. The observed symptom is that the whole `ContextInfo` never reaches the extension, which suggests the function responds with no arguments (or another field of `ContextInfo` is left unset and serialization drops the result). Maintainers will know the exact path better than I do. Notes on the two unchecked boxes above: - ungoogled-chromium: not tested, no build on hand. Since the patch above is inherited from `patches/ungoogled-chromium/`, this may well be an upstream issue rather than a Helium one. Please reroute if so. - Clean `--user-data-dir`: not tested, because the extension needs a signed-in Workspace account and an admin-enabled Endpoint Verification policy to do anything at all. On the Chrome check that is ticked: same machine, same account, same extension version. Chrome's extension storage holds a populated Browser Info record (`browserVersion`, `isRealtimeUrlCheckModeEnabled`) plus a `lastSyncTime`, and no such `SEVERE` entry. In Helium the same record never materializes: `[DeviceInfoService] [TRACE] Cached Browser Info: undefined`. Two other messages appear in the same log. Both look expected for a non-Chrome, non-cloud-managed browser and are not the cause of the failure, listing them only so they are not mistaken for the bug: ``` [NativeMessenger(ApiHelper)] [DEBUG] Failed to connect to 'com.google.endpoint_verification.api_helper'. Specified native messaging host not found. [ChromeDeviceInfoProvider] [WARNING] Error getting Device ID. Failed to retrieve the device id. ``` Impact: Helium cannot be used at all in a Google Workspace org that enforces context-aware access, since the device never gets verified. Note this is not a request to ship Safe Browsing. Returning a valid `ContextInfo` with the check mode reported as disabled, or surfacing a proper `lastError`, would be enough. Filed previously as #2330, closed for not following the template. Refiled with the template fields. Vulnerabilities ### 🔴 VULN-1 — Unfiltered argument forwarding → Chromium flag injection **Severity:** Medium · **Type:** CWE-150 (Improper Neutralization of Escape...) / flag-injection surface · **Location:** `0x14001C047`–`0x14001C045` loop in `ChromeProxy_wWinMain` Every argument after `argv[0]` is appended verbatim to the child command line: ```cpp // pseudo-decompile of the loop @ 0x14001C045 for (size_t i = 1; i < argv.size(); ++i) new_command_line.AppendArgNative(argv[i]); // <-- no allowlist/blocklist ``` If any actor controls how `chrome_proxy.exe` is invoked (it is the registered browser binary → protocol handlers, shortcuts, third-party integrations), the following classes of switches reach the browser unfiltered: ``` --gpu-launcher= --utility-cmd-prefix= --renderer-cmd-prefix= --no-sandbox --disable-web-security --load-extension= --user-data-dir= ``` → arbitrary command execution in browser child-process context. **Exploit sketch (local):** ```bat chrome_proxy.exe "https://example.org" --gpu-launcher^ "cmd.exe /c calc.exe #" ``` **Mitigation note:** upstream Chromium behaves identically; real-world abuse is partially mitigated inside `chrome.exe` (untrusted-launch switch sanitization). Recommended hardening: strip/deny-list dangerous switches before forwarding. --- ### 🟡 VULN-2 — No integrity verification of launched target **Severity:** Low/Medium · **Type:** CWE-494 (Download of Code Without Integrity Check) · **Locations:** `0x14001BE56` (path build), `0x140045F3E` (`CreateProcessW`) The launcher builds `\chrome.exe` and executes it without: 1. any signature or hash validation; 2. any `PathExists` pre-check (missing target ⇒ crash instead of graceful exit); 3. any ACL awareness — install root is user-writable: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\imput\Helium\Application`. Requires same-user write access to the application directory (or weak ACLs left by an elevated installer → install-time race/LPE class). --- ## 7. Description I recently downloaded the Helium browser and really liked the concept. However, the complete lack of cross-device sync or account backup was a total dealbreaker for me, and I ultimately had to delete the browser because of it. ### Who's implementing? - [x] I'm willing to implement this feature myself ### The problem I understand Helium is focused on privacy and ungoogled-chromium, but even an encrypted, self-hosted, or manual local sync file option would be a massive help. I would love to switch back to Helium once sync is supported! ### Possible solutions ### Suggested Immediate Workarounds For now, users can manually migrate the User Data profile folder (`\imput\Helium\User Data\`) across devices or automate it with tools like Syncthing. Relying on independent cross-platform extensions (like Bitwarden or Raindrop) also handles password and bookmark syncing externally. ### Long-Term Native Solutions 1. **Zero-Knowledge Sync Chain:** A pairing system using a secret passphrase or QR code (similar to Brave) to link devices without creating user accounts. 2. **Local Encrypted Vault Exports:** Automated backup files that can be saved to a user's private cloud (OneDrive, iCloud, Proton Drive). 3. **WebDAV / Nextcloud Support:** Allowing advanced users to link their own self-hosted servers for self-managed syncing. I'm glad to see commits regarding a "custom sync backend foundation" and "private vault format" in recent updates—highly looking forward to seeing native private sync implemented! ### Additional context Would it be possible to add account synchronization to the Helium browser? I think it would be a very useful feature, especially for keeping browser data and settings synchronized across different devices. Thank you for considering it! https://lens.google.com/upload ``` I understand that the presence of a URL in a binary does not by itself prove that the URL is ever contacted. I therefore tried to look at the actual runtime behaviour using standard Linux tools. The running Helium installation has multiple Chromium processes, including: ``` --type=utility --utility-sub-type=network.mojom.NetworkService ``` I can also observe active TCP connections belonging to Helium with: `sudo ss -tpn | grep '[h]elium'` For example, I observed connections such as: ``` helium,pid=111224 ↓ 48.222.183.128:443 ``` I then monitored network traffic while triggering the Lens functionality: ``` sudo tcpdump -i any -nn -tttt \ '(udp port 53 or tcp port 53 or tcp port 443)' ``` During my test, I did **not** observe a classical DNS request on port 53 for: `lens.google.com` I am deliberately **not** interpreting this as proof that Helium does not resolve or contact that hostname. Secure DNS / DNS-over-HTTPS can make a traditional port-53 capture incomplete, and HTTPS also prevents a simple packet capture from revealing the actual HTTP request path. So my question is simply about the intended purpose of the URL in the binary. **Could the Helium developers clarify:** 1. Is `https://lens.google.com/upload` part of Chromium functionality that is included in the Helium build? 2. Is this URL actually used by Helium's Lens integration? 3. If it is used, under what circumstances is a request made to it? 4. Is the request expected to originate directly from Helium, or from another Chromium component? 5. Is there a relevant source-code location that explains why this URL is present? **I am not claiming that Helium is secretly communicating with Google.** The presence of the string alone does not establish that, and my network test did not establish such a connection either. I am simply trying to understand why this endpoint is present in the binary and whether it is expected to be used by Helium. If this is inherited Chromium functionality, a pointer to the relevant Chromium source/component would also be very helpful. Thanks!
